main_text.p: diffyllabis et polyfyllabis, vocales longæ nunquam ufurpentur nisi in syllabis simplicibus aut ab initio compositis ut in דְּבָרִים, דָּבָר [?], nec breves nisi in compositis, nisi penultima afficiatur accentu Grammatico.
Cum vero in monosyllabis, & in polysyllabarum fine interdum reperitur vocalis longa, fit hoc ex caufa speciali. vide Capell. in Punct. Arcan. lib. 1. c. 13.

ה & י in fine vocis, poft Tsere Chirec longum, Cholem & Schurec, sæpe ad faciliorem pronunciationem assumunt Pathach, quod ante eas rapide & quasi furtim pronunciatur, unde vocatur Pathach genubha, seu furtim ascitum, ut מַשְׂכִּיחַ mafchiach. רוּחַ ruach יָדוּחַ [?] jaduah.
ה cum Mappic, idem aliquando imitatur, ut גָּבוֹאָה [?] Gaboah. Chaldaeis eadem syllabæ ratio est quæ Hebraeis.

In Bibliis voces quæ circellum supra se habent, aliter leguntur quàm scribuntur, Cùm enim Masorethæ ex M.SS. antiquis varias lectiones annotarunt, lectionem unam in textu reliquerunt, alteram in margine posuerunt, quam ut plurimum meliorem judicabant, & hujus vocales textui addebant, unde legunt prout in margine notatur, ut Psal. 9. 13. in textu est עֲנוִים [?] at in margine עֲנָיִים [?] unde ratione punctorum legitur mansuetorum at ratione literarum esset afflictorum עֲנוּיִים [?] Hujusmodi varias lectiones vocant Keri & Kethib, lectio & scriptio.
Notandum etiam nomen Tetragrammaton יְהוָה [?] si punctetur hoc modo יְהֹוִה [?] legendum אֱלֹהִים

page.notes: Hebrew vowel points and some Hebrew words (e.g. in the Psalm 9:13 example and the Chaldee example) are doubtful at this scan resolution and are marked [?]. The text in the Psalm 9:13 passage is partly reconstructed from the surrounding Latin and should be checked against the image. Long s is written as plain s throughout. "ascitum" is read from "afcitum" (long s). No marginal notes, headings, or catchword are present.
